title: Writ Petition — Quo Warranto (Article 226/32)
description: Writ of quo warranto challenging the authority of a person holding a substantive public office of statutory or constitutional character without legal qualification or in breach of the appointing statute.

locus_basis.label: Locus standi basis (quo warranto allows stranger locus)

impugned_appointee.label: Name of Person Holding Disputed Public Office

statute_creating_office.label: Statute / Constitutional Provision creating the office (section + Act)

relief_sought.label: Specific Relief — ouster of usurper from public office

mandatory_clauses: Cause title with petitioner v. impugned appointee + appointing authority + Union/State
Jurisdiction clause — Article 226 (HC) or Article 32 (SC) [Art 32 rarely successful — fundamental right link required]
Locus standi paragraph — stranger / concerned citizen permissible for quo warranto
Identification of public office — must be substantive (not employment under contract)
Statutory source of office — quote provision creating office
Particulars of impugned appointment (date, order number, gazette notification)
Ground — how appointee lacks qualification, suffers disqualification, or appointment is otherwise unlawful
No alternative remedy / urgency of ouster
Prayer for writ of quo warranto ousting appointee + declaring office vacant

prompt_context.system_role: You are drafting a Writ of Quo Warranto under Article 226/32. Quo warranto lies only when: (1) the office is a substantive public office of constitutional or statutory character (NOT private employment, NOT contractual posts, NOT mere honorary positions), (2) the office is held by a person who lacks the prescribed qualification or suffers a prescribed disqualification or whose appointment is in breach of statute, (3) the office is permanent in nature. Cite University of Mysore v. C.D. Govinda Rao AIR 1965 SC 491 (test for public office), Rajesh Awasthi v. Nand Lal Jaiswal (2013) 1 SCC 501, Hari Bansh Lal v. Sahodar Prasad Mahto (2010) 9 SCC 655. Locus is liberal — even a stranger may approach for quo warranto in public interest. The court inquires into the legal authority of the holder, not the merits of the appointment decision.
prompt_context.tone: formal, constitutional, focused on statutory authority
style_notes: Quote the statute/rule creating the office and prescribing qualifications verbatim
Annex copy of impugned appointment order/gazette notification (Annexure P-1)
Plead that office is 'public' and 'substantive' explicitly

Frame prayer as 'issue a writ of quo warranto or any other appropriate writ, order or direction calling upon respondent no. ___ to show by what authority he/she holds the office of ___ and on failure thereof to oust him/her from the said office'
Address why locus exists even if petitioner is a stranger

relevantActs.notes: Quo warranto under Art. 32 difficult unless fundamental right link
Where eligibility/disqualification is prescribed by rules

filing_checklist: Memo of writ petition with index, synopsis, list of dates
Affidavit in support sworn before Oath Commissioner
Annexure: copy of appointment order / gazette notification — mandatory
Annexure: copy of statute creating office + qualification rules
Annexure: documents showing appointee lacks qualification or suffers disqualification
Service copies — to appointee, appointing authority, State/UoI as proforma
Public interest litigation compliance if filed as PIL (HC Rules)

If court=Supreme Court and article=32, fundamental right linkage must be pleaded
Impugned appointee must be made respondent in personal capacity, not just office
